items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s my friend. ... We were good friends for a minute. ... he was a good friend, Gene Gammage.

ctx.x: Did you have preferences as to what you played? Or did it make a difference what the kit was?

Nah, that’s just part of learning the drums and what they were doing at the time. You listen to Max and see what kind of solo he just put out or something, and go through it – try to go through that, analyze that, and try to see how much of that you could play if you wanted to. Things like that. It was Kenny Clarke. It was Max. It was Art Blakey. There was a lot of guys I can’t call the names of. Shadow Wilson. There was a lot of guys. I got a tee-shirt on with about 150 guys that I knew them all, and I can’t…
Were jam sessions a part of all of this, overlaid to all of this?
